searchText: some notes from the eth2 call today : https://hackmd.io/@benjaminion/SkfYVnJ68#Validator-key-hygiene Plan is to continue discussion here and on EIPs and to schedule a call for nextweek make sure to share any recommendations that come out of client audits One relevant thing that came up in our external review is to consider using `aragon2id` for the key derivation function (EIP-2535). This EIP currently specifies two KDFs, `PBKDF2` and `scrypt`. - `PBKDF2` computations require very little RAM, making it potentially vulnerable to bruteforce attacks with GPUs. - `scrypt` is a better alternative, but as mentioned by Carl I think, it takes large amounts of memory (and the data-dependent memory accesses might make it vulnerable to side-channel attacks). `Argon2` won the 2015 password hashing competition. I know <@!361447803194441738> had planned to commenting on the relevant EIP with this finding, but thought I'd mention it here too 🙂 FYI we have a short blurb on key management here: https://lighthouse-book.sigmaprime.io/key-managment.html Something that I've noticed during converstations is ambiguity around the term "wallet": I tend to use wallet to refer to an EIP-2386 "walletstore", which is just a single JSON file that contains (a) an encrypted seed and (b) a nonce (`nextaccount`) that allow for churning out validators incrementally as per EIP-2334 (Deterministic Account Hierarchy) I've noticed "wallet" also being used to refer to an ethdo concept of a "wallet", which (I think) is a directory which contains an EIP-2386 walletstore and zero or more EIP-2335 keystores (and an index). I think this naming system could be improved. We have a "keystore" which holds "keys" but the "walletstore" doesn't hold "wallets", its the other way around. Regardless, I think a VC that wants to sign consensus messages needs not be concerned with either concept of a "wallet". It just has `n` keystores loaded from some arbitrary directory structure.

excerpts.author: ethzed
excerpts.content:
One relevant thing that came up in our external review is to consider using `aragon2id` for the key derivation function (EIP-2535). This EIP currently specifies two KDFs, `PBKDF2` and `scrypt`. 

- `PBKDF2` computations require very little RAM, making it potentially vulnerable to bruteforce attacks with GPUs.
- `scrypt` is a better alternative, but as mentioned by Carl I think, it takes large amounts of memory (and the data-dependent memory accesses might make it vulnerable to side-channel attacks).

`Argon2` won the 2015 password hashing competition. I know <@!361447803194441738> had planned to commenting on the relevant EIP with this finding, but thought I'd mention it here too 🙂

I've noticed "wallet" also being used to refer to an ethdo concept of a "wallet", which (I think) is a directory which contains an EIP-2386 walletstore and zero or more EIP-2335 keystores (and an index).
